newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury 5-year notes seen yielding 6.33 pct.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury 5-year notes seen yielding 6.33 pct.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury's auction of $12.5 billion in 5-year notes on Wednesday is expected to produce a yield near 6.33 percent, dealers said.
At 1246 EST/1746 GMT, yields on the five-year notes were quoted at 6.325 percent in when-issued trade.
The bidding deadline for the notes is 1300 EST/1800 GMT and results are expected around 1345 EST/1845 GMT.
Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A., said it was hard to get a firm handle on how the auction would go.
"You get your customer books that make or break your action at two minutes before one o'clock," he said.
But Stiles said that since prices have cheapened since Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan delivered his hawkish Humphrey-Hawkins testimony earlier, the auction could benefit.
"My hunch is that it won't be so bad, given this rate back-up," said Stiles. "There's some potential for short-covering."
